Management Basics for Nurses

Management basics for nurses — functions of management, types of managers, decision making and delegation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List the functions of management
  • Differentiate levels of management
  • Describe decision making in nursing
  • Explain delegation and accountability

In simple words

Management is getting work done through people and resources, safely and on time. Nursing management applies the same ideas to people, care and safety.

Functions of management

Function What it means in the ward
Planning Set objectives and plan the duty roster, supplies and care plans
Organising Group tasks, set roles, arrange equipment and staffing
Staffing Recruit, train and allocate the right people
Directing Guide, motivate, communicate and supervise
Controlling Monitor standards, audits, budgets and quality
Coordinating Align nursing, medical, laboratory and support services

Levels of management

  • Top-level — policies, budgets, organisational goals
  • Middle-level — nursing superintendent, deputy nursing superintendent; interpret policy for units
  • Front-line (first-line) — ward in-charge, charge nurse; direct supervision of care

Decision making steps

  1. Identify and define the problem
  2. Gather information and analyse
  3. List possible options and weigh consequences
  4. Decide and prepare an action plan
  5. Implement, supervise and evaluate

Delegation

  • Assign the right task to the right person with clear instructions
  • Delegate tasks, not accountability
  • Explain, check understanding, give authority and support
  • Review results and give feedback

🔴 Delegate the task, keep the accountability

When a nurse in-charge delegates a dressing or feeding, the accountability for safe care stays with her. Delegation means checking, supervising and giving feedback, not simply handing off duties.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Functions of management: planning, organising, staffing, directing, controlling, coordinating.
  2. Front-line management is done by ward in-charge and charge nurse.
  3. Decision making steps: problem, information, options, decision, evaluation.
  4. Delegation does not transfer accountability.
  5. Delegate the right task to the right person with clear instructions.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Middle management interprets policies for units.
  2. Effective delegation saves time and builds staff competence.
  3. Records, reports and feedback are part of control.
  4. Policies give standard behaviour for similar situations.
  5. Nurses also manage time, materials and supplies.

📌 Memory trick

Functions = P-O-S-D-C — Plan, Organise, Staff, Direct, Control.

60-second revision

  • Management: getting work done through people safely.
  • Five functions: planning, organising, staffing, directing, controlling.
  • Three levels: top, middle and front-line.
  • Decision making: define, gather, choose, act, evaluate.
  • Delegate the task but keep the accountability.

Test yourself

Policies are useful because they:

Answer: B. Policies give consistent, standard guidance so that similar situations are handled the same way.

Which is a function of management?

Answer: A. Planning is a core management function that sets objectives and methods.

Ward in-charge supervision is an example of:

Answer: B. Front-line management directly supervises daily care and staff work in a unit.

After delegation, accountability lies with:

Answer: B. Delegation transfers the task, not accountability; the delegator remains answerable.

The first step in decision making is:

Answer: B. Defining the problem clearly is the first step before options can be weighed.
